name: @betanyc/ny-data-registry-mcp

tools.name: find_sources
tools.description: Find New York open data portals and sources (state, county, city, agency, library, nonprofit) in BetaNYC's registry by topic, name or place. Returns each source's portal URL, platform family, API type, dataset count, status and last-verified date. Searches portal names and notes, not dataset titles (use search_datasets for datasets). Default status filter is 'live'.

place.description: County, city, NYC borough or region, e.g. 'Erie County', 'Buffalo', 'Brooklyn', 'Capital Region'

tier.description: 1 statewide portals, 2 state agencies/authorities, 3 local government, 4 nonprofit/academic

has_api.description: Only sources with (true) or without (false) a queryable API

status.description: Default 'live'. Use 'any' to include no-portal, dead and UNCONFIRMED rows

tools.name: list_sources_for_place
tools.description: Everything the registry knows for one New York place (county, one of the 62 cities, an NYC borough, or a region): its own portal(s), sources for cities inside it, regional sources, and statewide sources that cover it. Says plainly whether the place has a portal, was checked and has none ('no-portal-exists'), or is not in the registry ('not-in-registry', which means unchecked, not absent).

include_statewide.description: List the statewide sources too (default true)

limit.description: Most rows in each list (own, within, regional, statewide). Default 25

tools.name: how_to_query
tools.description: How to get data from one registry source: its endpoint (copied verbatim, never guessed), API type, whether a key is needed and which env var holds it, an example request, and which MCP server to hand off to (the `socrata` MCP with the right domain, or the matching @betanyc MCP). Flags UNCONFIRMED, undocumented, gated, dead and no-portal rows.

registry_id.description: Government body id from BetaNYC/ny-gov-web-registry. Several sources can share one; then the reply lists them

entity.description: Entity name, e.g. 'NYS Department of Health'

limit.description: When several rows match: most to list. Default 25

offset.description: When several rows match: skip this many (next_offset)

tools.name: check_source
tools.description: Live check of one source's portal URL: exactly one request (no retry), redirects reported (not followed), HTTP status, response time, and whether that matches the registry's status. A url is never fetched itself: it picks a registry row by host and path, and when no row clearly matches, the rows on that host are listed and nothing is fetched. Never calls key-required or account-gated sources, and reports a bot block rather than working around it.

url.description: A portal URL; matched to its registry row by host

tools.name: registry_info
tools.description: Registry row counts by status, tier and platform family, and how many rows carry a registry_id; which copy of the master list of government bodies (BetaNYC/ny-gov-web-registry) is loaded and which row ids it lacks; when the registry was generated and where this copy came from (bundled or refreshed from GitHub Pages); unmapped platform strings; and the harvested index's size and last harvest date. index_status says how old the index is, whether automatic updates are on (and if not, which setting turned them off), and what the last update check found.

tools.name: search_datasets
tools.description: Search dataset titles, descriptions, tags and column names across the harvested Socrata and ArcGIS portals in New York (needs the harvested index). Filter by topic, place, portal, platform family, download format (csv, geojson, shapefile, kml, api, xlsx) or last-updated date. topic is one of 24 shared topics (list_topics), assigned from each dataset's own categories, tags and department; a dataset can have several. Give a query, a topic, or both; a topic alone lists that topic, most-viewed first. Rows carry their topic ids. One call gives the whole answer. total_matches is the true number of matching datasets. When they all fit, the reply lists them. When they do not, the reply counts every match by portal (auto_grouped: true; top titles when room; groups_size_note says what was cut), lists the best-ranked rows that fit, and writes every match to a CSV (export.path, export.rows; also a resource_link). Use group_by to summarize by entity, county or platform_family instead. Rows are compact (id, name, portal, type, update date, link, formats); detail: 'full' adds description, API endpoint, views, column count and, for Socrata, the domain + 4x4 to hand to the `socrata` MCP. Replies aim for about 20 KB. Each reply also lists registry portals the index does not search, so no result is not proof that no data exists. When the index is more than 14 days old (NY_DATA_INDEX_STALE_DAYS), the reply carries index_note saying so and how to update it.

query.description: e.g. 'rodent', 'tax parcels', 'lead service lines'. Optional when topic is given

topic.description: One of the 24 shared topics (list_topics has names and counts), e.g. 'housing', 'transportation', 'elections'

place.description: County, city, borough or region. Statewide portals are always included

portal.description: source_id, registry_id (every site of that government) or part of a portal name

format.description: csv, json, geojson, shapefile, kml, api, arcgis, xlsx, geopackage, pdf

limit.description: Most rows to list in the reply. Default 10. More matches than this are summarized by portal and written to the CSV. Not with group_by

offset.description: Rarely needed: skip this many ranked rows to page by hand (next_offset). Turns off the auto-summary and the automatic CSV. Not with group_by

group_by.description: Group every match by portal, entity, county or platform_family, with counts and top titles per group, instead of a page of results

top_per_group.description: Titles listed per group with group_by. Default 3

export.description: 'auto' (default): write the CSV of every match when the reply cannot list them all. 'always' or 'never'

tools.name: list_topics
tools.description: The 24 shared topics for New York open data, with how many datasets and portals each has in the harvested index, and the share of datasets with at least one topic. Topics are built from the categories, tags and departments the portals already use; a dataset can have several. Use a topic id with search_datasets. Also links the crosswalk (each portal label and its topics), published with every index.

portal.description: Count one portal only: source_id or part of a portal name

tools.name: get_dataset_columns
tools.description: Column names, field names, types and descriptions for one dataset from the index, plus every distribution (format + URL), license, publisher, extent and per-field provenance (from the portal vs derived here). With standard 'croissant' (read by AI and ML tools) or 'dcat-us' (DCAT-US 3.0, read by government catalogs and data.gov), returns the dataset's description in that standard instead, with which required fields the portal did not give. A license is never inferred: where the portal gives none, a terms page may be linked, labeled 'terms page, not a license'.

dataset.description: dataset_id from search_datasets, a Socrata 4x4, an ArcGIS item id, or the dataset URL

standard.description: Return the description as Croissant 1.1 ('croissant') or DCAT-US 3.0 ('dcat-us') instead of the column list

tools.name: find_joinable
tools.description: Datasets that share a join key with this one, grouped by key: BBL, BIN, borough, community district, council district, census tract, SWIS, FIPS, ZIP. Uses a curated key-column map, not raw column-name equality.

dataset.description: dataset_id, Socrata 4x4, ArcGIS item id or URL

column.description: Limit to one key (a field name in the dataset, or a key label like 'BBL')

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Datasets added, changed or removed in the index since a date, and datasets whose portal says they were updated since then. Optional portal filter. For changes to this server itself (new tools, fixes, corrections), use whats_changed instead.

portal.description: source_id, registry_id (every site of that government) or part of a portal name

limit.description: Most rows in each list. Default 50

tools.name: whats_changed
tools.description: What has changed in this server, its data and its website, newest first, from the project's WHATS-CHANGED.md: new tools and pages, new data, data fixes, and corrections when BetaNYC published something wrong. Each correction says what to re-check if you used the old numbers. Call this before relying on a figure you got from this server earlier, or when a user asks whether something was fixed. Filter with since (YYYY-MM-DD; also keeps older entries that have an update on or after that date) and tag (Site, Data, MCP or Correction).

since.description: Only changes on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD

tag.description: Only changes with this tag: Site, Data, MCP or Correction (any case; answers use these spellings). Correction lists every correction.

tools.name: about_betanyc
tools.description: Who built this server and how to reach them: BetaNYC, a project of the Fund for the City of New York. Returns what BetaNYC is, links to its events, newsletter and donation page, where to report a bug in this server or ask for a new feature (this server's GitHub issues), and this server's name and version.

tools.name: about_data
tools.description: Where this server's data comes from and how far to trust it. For each kind of data: who publishes it and a link, whether it is an official record (only data its publisher published and BetaNYC did not modify is; data BetaNYC modified or produced is not), how it was gathered, what BetaNYC did to it (for example cleaned it, matched it to addresses, joined it with other data, or counted it), how current it is on this server, what it covers and what is missing, the terms of use and the credit line to print, where to check a figure at the official record, where to report an error (to BetaNYC when BetaNYC modified or produced the data, to the publisher for the original records, and to this server's issues for a bug), which tools use it, and corrections that touched it. Call it whenever someone asks where an answer comes from, how current or accurate it is, or how to check or cite it. topic narrows it to one kind of data, or to the data behind one tool (give the tool's name). For who built this server, use about_betanyc. Topics on this server: portal-registry, portal-check, government-bodies, places, portal-catalogs, catalog-health-data-ny, catalog-nys-gis-clearinghouse, catalog-open-ny, catalog-adirondack-park-agency, catalog-dec-gis-services, catalog-environmental-bond-act, catalog-nysdec-arcgis-online, catalog-ny-geographic-information-gateway, catalog-nysdot-gis, catalog-nys-elevation-data, catalog-nys-geohub, catalog-nys-its-gis-services, catalog-nys-orthoimagery, catalog-nys-parks-arcgis-online, catalog-albany-county, catalog-columbia-county, catalog-greene-county, catalog-warren-county, catalog-washington-county, catalog-cayuga-county, catalog-city-of-syracuse, catalog-city-of-utica, catalog-cortland-county, catalog-oswego-county, catalog-dutchess-county, catalog-orange-county, catalog-sullivan-county, catalog-ulster-county, catalog-city-of-mount-vernon, catalog-nassau-county, catalog-nyc-open-data, catalog-nyc-dcp-mapping, catalog-nycmaphub, catalog-putnam-county, catalog-suffolk-county, catalog-westchester-county, catalog-city-of-watertown, catalog-essex-county, catalog-broome-county, catalog-city-of-ithaca, catalog-otsego-county, catalog-steuben-county, catalog-tioga-county, catalog-tompkins-county, catalog-cattaraugus-county, catalog-chautauqua-county, catalog-city-of-buffalo, catalog-city-of-rochester, catalog-genesee-county, catalog-livingston-county, catalog-monroe-county, catalog-ontario-county, catalog-wayne-county, catalog-wyoming-county, catalog-yates-county, catalog-suny-cortland, catalog-syracuse-university, catalog-lehman-bronx-information-portal, catalog-cornell-cugir, catalog-university-of-rochester, hand-kept, topics, coverage, join-keys, standard-descriptions.

topic.description: A source id, or any tool's name for the data behind it. Any case. Default: a short list of all sources; "all": each in full.

annotations.title: Where this server's data comes from

instructions: New York open data portals and their datasets, from BetaNYC's registry and a nightly index of the portals' catalogs. It describes datasets; it does not hold the data itself. Source rows (find_sources, list_sources_for_place, how_to_query, check_source) and dataset rows carry registry_id when the row has one: the id of the row's government body in BetaNYC/ny-gov-web-registry, for joining the two. Source rows also carry runs_it, the government body that runs the site (name, government_level, classification, website), looked up by registry_id in that list; null when the row has no id, found: false when the list lacks it. runs_it_source says which copy of the list answered. Every registry and index answer carries data_source: the source, its publisher, a link and how current it is, a cite line to quote, and its about_data_topic. Rows from several sources list each in data_sources. When someone asks where an answer's data comes from, how current or accurate it is, whether it is official, or how to check, cite, or correct it, call about_data (with a topic for one kind of data or one tool) and answer from it, naming the source and its publisher. about_data gives each source one of three answers on whether it is official. "Publisher: … BetaNYC did not modify it." means it is the publisher's own record. "BetaNYC modified this data" means this copy is not the official record; say what BetaNYC did, name the official record and give its link. "BetaNYC produced this" means BetaNYC built or collected it, and it is not an official record either. Never call data official when BetaNYC modified or produced it. For who built this server, call about_betanyc; for recent fixes and corrections, call whats_changed.
